bibliography.title: Just-In-Time Reinforcement Learning: Continual Learning in LLM Agents Without Gradient Updates
bibliography.venue_line: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026

source_files.read_scope: All 27 physical PDF pages; no separate supplementary file associated with this paper_id was found.

page_map.boundary_note: Main narrative ends with Acknowledgement on p. 9; References begin later on p. 9 and continue through p. 10; Appendix begins p. 11.

abstract_sentences.text: While Large Language Model (LLM) agents excel at general tasks, they inherently struggle with continual adaptation due to the frozen weights after deployment.
Conventional reinforcement learning (RL) offers a solution but incurs prohibitive computational costs and the risk of catastrophic forgetting.
We introduce Just-In-Time Reinforcement Learning (JitRL), a training-free framework that enables test-time policy optimization without any gradient updates.
JitRL maintains a dynamic, non-parametric memory of experiences and retrieves relevant trajectories to estimate action advantages on-the-fly.
These estimates are then used to directly modulate the LLM’s output logits.

evidence.anchor: directly modulate the LLM’s output logits

abstract_sentences.text: We theoretically prove that this additive update rule is the exact closed-form solution to the KL-constrained policy optimization objective.
Extensive experiments on WebArena and Jericho demonstrate that JitRL establishes a new state-of-the-art among training-free methods.

Crucially, JitRL outperforms the performance of computationally expensive fine-tuning methods (e.g., WebRL) while reducing monetary costs by over 30×, offering a scalable path for continual learning agents.
The code is available at https://github.com/liushiliushi/JitRL.

experimental_design.name: Research questions
experimental_design.description: Four questions cover main performance, generalization across unseen tasks/backbones, qualitative decision correction, and key-component impact.

experimental_design.name: Benchmarks
experimental_design.description: WebArena and Jericho; Jericho uses Library, Zork1, and Zork3.

experimental_design.name: Training-free backbone
experimental_design.description: Main JitRL/training-free comparisons use Gemini-2.5-flash; RQ2 additionally tests GPT-5-mini and DeepSeek-V3.2.

experimental_design.name: Weight-update baselines
experimental_design.description: WebArena compares SFT/WebRL on Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct; Jericho uses task-specific Qwen3-32B GRPO checkpoints.

experimental_design.name: WebArena aggregation
experimental_design.description: Each task is executed for L=5 sequential episodes; Avg averages T×5 binary task episodes and Final takes the fifth episode.

experimental_design.name: Jericho aggregation
experimental_design.description: Average game score is over 50 episodes and Final is the last-episode score.

experimental_design.name: WebArena hyperparameters
experimental_design.description: Table 11 lists step limit 10, seed 0, temperature 0.8, candidate actions 3, gamma 0.1, k 10, retrieval thresholds, lambda 0.05, and alpha 5.

experimental_design.name: Jericho hyperparameters
experimental_design.description: Table 10 lists step limit 60, 50 episodes, temperature 0.8, candidate actions 3, gamma 0.5, k 10, similarity threshold 0.95, lambda 0.65, and alpha 5.

experimental_design.name: State/retrieval/action implementation
experimental_design.description: Appendix F specifies URL regularization and Jaccard retrieval for WebArena, hybrid state/history retrieval for Jericho, action normalization, and valid-action constraints.

experimental_design.name: Held-out and disjoint-memory controls
experimental_design.description: Table 2 uses held-out WebArena-Lite; Table 5 restricts retrieval to memory from disjoint tasks.

experimental_design.description: Appendices I/J offer an on-the-fly same-Llama-8B comparison, a separate-training same-Llama-70B comparison, and a same-Qwen3-32B Jericho comparison.

claim_closure.claim: Frozen LLMs can continually adapt without gradient updates.
claim_closure.method_response: Memory retrieval estimates advantages and Eq. (10) shifts logits.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Sequential WebArena/Jericho measurements and Figure 3 show gains in the tested regimes.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion restates test-time adaptation of frozen LLMs.

claim_closure.claim: The additive logit rule is the exact KL-regularized optimum.
claim_closure.method_response: Eq. (8)-(10) formulate and implement the objective.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Appendix B derives Eqs. (13)-(21) and Theorem 4.1 states the result.

claim_closure.claim: Values, advantages, and the induced policy are consistent under nonstationary policies.
claim_closure.method_response: The estimator is kNN-based over memory and the policy is a continuous softmax mapping.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Appendices C/D prove tracking under C.1-C.6 but the experiment does not directly validate those assumptions.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion does not restate the assumptions.

claim_closure.claim: JitRL is state of the art among the paper's training-free baselines.
claim_closure.method_response: The method specifies a shared test-time memory/logit mechanism.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Tables 1, 3, 4, and 5 provide task-level comparisons but no independent-run uncertainty.

claim_closure.claim: JitRL outperforms expensive weight-update methods while reducing cost by over 30x.
claim_closure.method_response: It avoids changing theta while retaining a KL-form policy update.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 2 and Table 9 support the headline comparison/cost, while same-backbone Table 13 is lower than WebRL in its offline setting.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion repeats the claim without the same-backbone qualification.

claim_closure.claim: The mechanism generalizes across models and disjoint tasks.
claim_closure.method_response: State abstraction and retrieved actions are specified in the method and Appendix F.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Tables 4-6 cover selected backbones/domains; use of cross-task memory does not directly identify abstract procedural knowledge.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion does not separately revisit the cross-task result.

limitations.name: Candidate-action coverage
limitations.description: JitRL re-weights actions proposed by the frozen base model and cannot discover never-generated actions.

limitations.name: Evaluator credit assignment
limitations.description: Inaccurate LLM evaluator step-wise rewards make advantage estimates inaccurate and may degrade policy quality.

limitations.name: Text representation boundary
limitations.description: Text-based state representation/retrieval may fail on critical patterns that are hard to express textually, including spatial reasoning and time-series forecasting.

limitations.name: Deployment privacy
limitations.description: A memory bank storing real interactions may inadvertently capture sensitive user information.

limitations.name: Systematic failure study
limitations.description: No systematic failure-case study or failure-count denominator is reported.

adverse_presentation_strategies.description: Tables 7 and 17 explicitly select representative cases; the PDF gives no sampling denominator or selection rule in those tables.

adverse_presentation_strategies.name: Limitations after conclusion

lexical_rhetoric.counting_scope: Pages 1-8 main narrative selected from PDF text layer after excluding headers, title area, figures, tables, captions, references, and formula fragments; 3,721 retained raw tokens; case normalized but not lemmatized.
tokenization_risks: PDF line-end hyphenation produces fragments such as con-; hyphenated forms such as training-free and on-the-fly need canonical handling.
The counts intentionally retain singular/plural and logit/logits separately.

final_judgment.single_storyline: JitRL turns retrieved historical returns into local advantage estimates and uses a KL-regularized closed-form logit shift to adapt a frozen LLM at test time without gradient updates.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The visual mechanism, core equations and theorem statements, four research questions, principal benchmark comparisons, prompt-versus-logit ablation, neighbor-count figure, and cost table remain in the main body.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Proofs, pseudocode, full implementation/prompt/hyperparameter detail, same-setting controls, extra case studies, sensitivity/scalability studies, GRPO sweep, and cost derivation move to Appendix A-R.
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figure 2, Eqs. (7)-(10), and Table 8 form a tight mechanism-to-executable-update-to-controlled-contrast sequence.
final_judgment.largest_gap: The broad weight-update superiority wording is bounded by backbone/protocol differences and by the same-Llama-70B offline Table 13 where JitRL is below WebRL; primary result displays also lack repeated-run uncertainty.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For a no-gradient adaptation claim, connect history, a constrained action-distribution update, and a controlled alternative implementation in one continuous evidence chain.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: The rule applies only when useful candidate actions, state similarity, and local credit evidence are available; the paper itself identifies candidate coverage, evaluator accuracy, and text-state limits.
final_judgment.conclusion_new_claims: No new method or task-level numerical claim is introduced in the one-paragraph conclusion; it restates over-30x cost already asserted in the abstract and supported by Table 9.
